Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Miami FL
642 AM EST Sat Nov 21 2026

...New AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES...
Updated at 640 AM EST Sat Nov 21 2026

  - Patchy dense fog may lead to reduced visibilities across the
    interior and Southwest Florida early this morning.

  - Scattered thunderstorms possible this afternoon into early
    evening. Locally heavy rain may lead to urban and poor
    drainage flooding.

  - High risk of rip currents today for the Palm Beaches.

&&

.SHORT TERM...
(Today through Sunday)
Issued at 121 AM EST Sat Nov 21 2026

Early morning analysis shows an upper level shortwave over the 
region with the trough axis to our west over the eastern Gulf. 
Meanwhile a surface frontal boundary extends from the eastern Gulf 
cutting up through the center of the state and extends out into the 
western Atlantic, with multiple weak low pressure systems along the 
front. 

With light winds, clearing skies, and some low level moisture in 
place, some fog will be possible early this morning over the 
interior, with areas of locally dense fog most likely over portions 
of the southern Everglades. Will need to monitor this closely this 
morning to see if any headlines or statements will be needed.

The shortwave will lift up to the northeast today and global models 
and forecast soundings show above normal PWAT values continuing 
across South FL. With mid to late day diurnal instability, some 
scattered showers and thunderstorms are expected. While the flow is 
generally unidirectional, 500 mb temps will be in the bottom 10th 
percentile, and MUCAPE values in the middle of the afternoon will be 
around 2k J/kg. So an isolated strong to marginally severe storm is 
not out of the question, with large hail and strong wind gusts being 
the primary threat. Also, given the saturated soils across the east 
coast metro, any heavy rainfall will have the ability to create some 
urban and poor drainage issues, so WPC has a marginal risk for 
excessive rainfall today. High temperatures today will be in the low 
to mid 80s. Convection should quickly wane late tonight with the 
loss of daytime heating. Partly cloudy skies overnight with the 
potential of some patchy fog over the interior. Low temps will range 
from the upper 60s to lower 70s. 

On Sunday the shortwave will continue lifting to the northeast well 
away from the area and the upper level flow across the state will 
become more zonal. Some drier air will begin to filter into the area 
however some widely scattered showers will remain possible. High 
temps on Sunday will range from the low to mid 80s along and north 
of Alligator Alley, to mid and upper 80s south of the Alley. 

&&

.LONG TERM...
(Sunday night through Friday)
Issued at 121 AM EST Sat Nov 21 2026

Monday will be a transition day across South FL with dry conditions 
and plenty of sunshine. Then the next shortwave will exit from the 
SW US towards the Gulf on Tuesday and another front will approach 
the region from the west. This will increase shower and thunderstorm 
chances for Tuesday and Wednesday and may linger into early 
Thursday. Eventually the front will move off to the east and the 
shortwave will cross and move to our east into the Atlantic, 
bringing drier conditions for the end of the work week. 

Temperatures will be fairly comfortable during the upcoming work 
week with highs generally in the upper 70s to lower 80s. Low temps 
will be in the 60s/70s through mid week and then trending a bit 
cooler to the 50s/60s by the end of the week. 

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAFS)
Issued at 640 AM EST Sat Nov 21 2026

VFR conditions should prevail through the period. Light and
variable winds overnight will turn southwesterly after 14Z, with a
gradually increasing chance of SHRA/TSRA for all terminals this
afternoon. Impact timing remains uncertain; short-fuse TEMPOs 
will likely be needed. Winds become light and variable again
overnight before a westerly southwesterly breeze returns on
Sunday. 

&&

.MARINE...
Issued at 121 AM EST Sat Nov 21 2026

Gentle to moderate west to southwest breeze across the local waters 
today. Seas in the Gulf 2 ft or less, and 2-4 ft seas in the 
Atlantic waters. 

&&

.BEACHES...
Issued at 121 AM EST Sat Nov 21 2026

Lingering swell will result in a high risk of rip currents today for 
the Palm Beaches.

&&

TWOAT 

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
700 AM EST Sat Nov 21 2026

For the North Atlantic...Caribbean Sea and the Gulf of America:

Offshore of the Southeast U.S. Coast:
A large non-tropical low pressure area centered a few hundred miles 
east of northeastern Florida continues to produce disorganized 
showers and thunderstorms. The system is moving into an 
environment that will probably not be conducive for development of 
significant tropical or subtropical characteristics. 

Although the chances of tropical development continue to decrease, 
this large weather system is still expected to produce gusty winds, 
dangerous surf, rip currents, and coastal flooding along portions 
of the southeast and mid-Atlantic U.S. coasts into early next week. 
In addition, heavy rainfall and the threat of flash flooding will 
move northward over coastal portions of the Carolinas and the 
mid-Atlantic through the weekend. Interests along the U.S. 
East Coast should continue to monitor the progress of this system. 
Additional information on this system, including Gale Warnings, can 
be found in High Seas Forecasts issued by the National Weather 
Service, as well as products issued by your local National Weather 
Service forecast office.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...10 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...10 percent.

&&
High Seas Forecasts issued by the National Weather Service can be 
found under AWIPS header NFDHSFAT1, WMO header FZNT01 KWBC, and 
online at ocean.weather.gov/shtml/NFDHSFAT1.php

$$
